title: Logarithmic Relative Fluctuations in the Weakly Disordered Planar Ising Model
main_claim: Assuming deterministic critical-reference estimates from a companion paper (ReferenceIsing), for the square-lattice Ising model with i.i.d. bonds 1±ε, small fixed ε>0, at the physical β_c(ε) (the solution of sinh(2β(1-ε))sinh(2β(1+ε))=1), the relative second moment R_ε(r)=E[C²]/E[C]² of the quenched free spin correlation is (log r)^{1/4+o(1)}.

issues.location: Sec. coefficients, Lemma coef:profiles (bound on the formal mean profile m*_j) together with flow:mean-profile
issues.description: The flow comparison needs the formal mean profile m*_j, including its expanding thermal coordinate, to stay bounded uniformly in j. The paper derives this from a per-site bound ||H_{i,2}|| ≤ C r^{-2}, which comes from the exact single-insertion identity P H_2 = -1/2 P(H_1^2), and then sums over the C r^2 contributing sites. The argument is terse about how the slot sup-norm bound controls the thermal (charge) coordinate. That control is needed for the backward estimate z_j = L^{-1} z_{j+1} + ... with |z_N| ≤ C G_N. I see no error, only compressed justification.
issues.evidence: Lemma coef:profiles: 'Summing the second estimate in (coef:single-columns) proves the bound on m_j^*.' flow:mean-profile uses x*_N bounded to start the backward recursion.

issues.description: The whole result is conditional on deterministic reference inputs from the companion paper ReferenceIsing: even-function decay under conditioning, operator bounds, the energy–spin OPE coefficients (Lemma ref:ope), and charge functionals. I did not verify these. The paper states this dependence openly, so it is not circular.
issues.evidence: Abstract and Theorem 1.1: 'Assume the deterministic reference-model estimates of [ReferenceIsing]'.

coverage:
Read the introduction, coefficients, flow, marked, readout and transition sections in full, and the OPE lemma in the reference section. I did not audit the blocking and norms sections line by line; they hold the large-field and Taylor machinery and are taken on trust.

Checks done:
(1) Pair invariant charge (t_i+t_k+A t_i t_k)/(1+C t_i t_k): the degree-4 variance after the sign substitution is A²−4C, recomputed by hand.
(2) β_J=(1/2)Σ(ℓ²−4⟨ee⟩) with ⟨ee⟩~a²/|z|² and lattice sum Σ|z|^{-2}=2π log R gives −4πa² log r, so B0=4πa² log L.
(3) Marked coefficient: binom(q,2)·Σ a²/(4|z|²)=binom(q,2)(πa²/2) log r. This matches C_σσε=1/2 in CFT normalization. The ratio μ_q/B0=binom(q,2)/8 gives per-mark moments j^{q(q-1)/16} and two-point j^{q(q-1)/8}, in agreement with the Shankar/Ludwig prediction. For q=2 this gives (log r)^{1/4}.
(4) Flow reciprocal estimate (flow:relative-reciprocal), including the Σ s_j term relative to ḡ^{-1}+B0 k.
(5) Uniform second-moment bound, exponent (1/8+η/B0) < 1/4.
(6) First-moment error sum with exponent 11/8, giving C√ḡ.
(7) Joint-source bound s_J·J^{3/16}·J^{3/16}=J^{-1/8}.
(8) Buffer exponents: b²s_J=J^{-9/50}; Markov J^{-p/25}; exceptional-event Hölder J^{3/8−p/100}, which requires p>25.
(9) Subcritical arm union bound: n²·n^{8}·n^{-25}=n^{-15}.
(10) BKKKL/GJN threshold derivation and the monotone sequential representation.
(11) Torus Euler/duality identity r(A)+r(A*)=2 and the twist identity.
(12) Logit integration argument that t_*=0.
(13) Matching to physical β (log-sinh mean zero ⇔ self-dual curve) and the domination comparison for β>β_*.
sibling_notes: This paper is in the same family as rank92/159 (quenched SLE3 for the weak random-bond Ising model). Siblings checked the same torus-duality and OSSS-style transition identification: the self-dual identity v*=2/v, the 4-sector torus prefactor, and h*=0 via torus duality+OSSS. This paper re-proves those steps self-contained (twisted partition functions, BKKKL threshold, quenched-revealment OSSS), and its versions agree with the sibling findings.
